title: Wyoming Statutes, Title 27 - Labor and Employment, Chapter 4 - Wages
source_id: Wyo. Stat. Ann. tit. 27, ch. 4 (ss 27-4-101 through 27-4-508), comprising art. 1 In General (27-4-101 to 27-4-116), art. 2 Minimum Wages (27-4-201 to 27-4-204), art. 3 Equal Pay (27-4-301 to 27-4-304), art. 4 Prevailing Wages (27-4-401 to 27-4-413) and art. 5 Collection of Unpaid Wages (27-4-501 to 27-4-508)
verified_how: walked the LSO NXT table of contents (gateway.dll?f=xmlcontents&command=getchildren) down to 'TITLE 27 - LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT' > 'CHAPTER 4 - WAGES' and each of its five articles, whose first and last section catchlines read '27-4-101. Semimonthly payments required; method of payment; agricultural operations exempt; payment in case of labor dispute or temporary layoff.' ... '27-4-116. Employee not liable for dishonored check; penalty.'; '27-4-201. Definitions.' ... '27-4-204. Liability for unpaid minimum wage; suit for collection.'; '27-4-301. Definitions.' ... '27-4-304. Penalty for violations.'; '27-4-401. Short title.' ... '27-4-413. Inapplicability and exemptions.'; '27-4-501. Definitions.' ... '27-4-508. Agreements for reciprocal enforcement; of claim to another state.'. Repealed sections are shown in the same listing with a 'Repealed by Laws ...' catchline (e.g. '37-3-103. Repealed by Laws 1995, ch. 192, s 3.'), so the substantive catchlines above are live text. Currency: the LSO's Statutes Download page states 'This version of the Wyoming Statutes contains changes from the 2026 Budget Session and reflects the contents of the statutes as they exist as of July 1, 2026'; the NXT infobase I browsed is the one labelled '2026 Wyoming Statutes' (the register also keeps 2020-2025 as separate historical infobases). Official title PDF at https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title27.pdf.
notes: Covers pay frequency, method of payment, pay on quitting or discharge (27-4-104 'Payment of employee quitting or discharged and suit for wages; generally', with the penalty at 27-4-105), the state minimum wage, equal pay, prevailing wages on public works, and the Labor Standards route for collecting unpaid wages. Wyoming's own minimum wage in art. 2 sits below the federal floor, so the federal FLSA (29 U.S.C. ch. 8) governs most private employment - worth saying in the subject README.
